summary: Iteration-13 focused re-test of FIX A (illustration visibility across 4 viewports), FIX B (hero illustration swap), FIX C (favicon), plus regression sweep of public routes and backend smoke. Backend + favicon assets: 13/13 pytest cases pass (test_iteration13_smoke.py) covering /favicon.ico, /favicon-32x32.png, /favicon-16x16.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /logo192.png, /logo512.png all 200 with image content-type, manifest.json has exactly 3 icons (favicon.ico + logo192.png + logo512.png both with purpose 'any maskable'), index.html head contains rel=icon + apple-touch-icon + mask-icon links, /api/health, /api/admin-login (super-admin), /api/admin returns summary.breakdown.orqyne_pilots, /api/newsletter new+duplicate, /api/contact leadType=orqyne_pilot. Frontend illustration measurements via getBoundingClientRect (chip vs frame vs core-card vs chip): at 1920x1080, 1440x900, 768x1024 all five diagrams (hero-method-diagram, how-orbit-diagram, experience-visual IT-Services tab, experience-visual Canvas tab, about-orbit-diagram) return clipped=[], hitCore=[], overlap=[] — PERFECT. HOWEVER at the required 390x844 mobile viewport, every single diagram fails: labels are clipped by the rounded frame AND vertical chips overlap the central core card. WorkflowSpine.js is deleted and grep -r 'WorkflowSpine' /app/frontend/src returns no hits, so no missing-import error anywhere. Products Canvas tab click triggers re-render of experience-visual with the Canvas chips (Approvals/Automations/Business Pulse/Documents/Money impact/Access) confirmed programmatically.

ui_bugs.component: OrbitDiagram (hero-method-diagram, how-orbit-diagram, experience-visual IT tab, experience-visual Canvas tab, about-orbit-diagram)
ui_bugs.issue: At 390x844 mobile viewport, labels are CLIPPED by the rounded 4:3 frame AND vertical chips OVERLAP the central core card. Measurements (chip vs frame vs core rect): hero-method-diagram clipped=['1 Diagnose'] hitCore=['4 Govern']; how-orbit-diagram clipped=['Dependencies','Reporting'] hitCore=['Resources','Adoption']; experience-visual (IT Services) clipped=['Dependencies','Decisions'] hitCore=['Vendors']; experience-visual (Canvas) clipped=['Automations','Business Pulse'] hitCore=['Access']; about-orbit-diagram clipped=['AI readiness'] hitCore=['Decisions']. This is the exact obstruction/clipping bug FIX A was supposed to fix — desktop is now clean but mobile regressed. Root cause: OrbitDiagram uses fixed percentage radii (RING={x:36,y:40}) plus fixed pixel chip label widths and a fixed max-w-[9.5rem]=152px core card. At container width ~350px the horizontal chip label runs off the frame edge and the vertical chips fall on top of the core card whose relative footprint is now ~44% of the frame width instead of ~15% at 1920.

action_items: Fix OrbitDiagram responsiveness at ≤430px. Options: (a) shrink the core card / reduce max-w to ~7rem AND clamp chip label max-width with truncate on mobile, (b) drop RING radii on narrow widths (e.g. RING={x:30,y:34} below 640px), or (c) render a stacked mobile variant instead of the ellipse. Confirm chip.right<=frame.right, chip.bottom<=frame.bottom, and chip does not intersect the core card rect at width 390.

Main agent's previous verification claimed clipped=[] hitCore=[] at 390 for all four diagrams — that measurement was NOT reproducible; ensure the check-script actually asserts against the core card getBoundingClientRect and against ALL chip elements after the tab switch.
critical_code_review_comments: OrbitDiagram.layout() rotates the chip ring only when a chip is within 20° of the horizontal — this helps horizontal clipping on 4:3 but does nothing for the vertical chips (12 o'clock / 6 o'clock) which are the ones now landing on the core card at mobile.

The core card uses max-w-[9.5rem] (152px) which is a fixed pixel width; on a 350px wide frame that is 43% of the frame — the ring at 36% x-radius CANNOT clear it. This is an intrinsic geometry conflict at narrow widths that needs a responsive breakpoint.
Favicon set (index.html links + manifest.json 3 icons + all 6 static files served) is correctly wired and rendered by the browser — FIX C is fully verified.

WorkflowSpine.js file removed and no remaining imports in /app/frontend/src — FIX B is fully verified on desktop; the hero right column now renders hero-method-diagram with the 4 numbered chips as specified.

All 6 favicon files and manifest.json are served correctly and the browser resolves link[rel=icon]. The remaining bug is purely CSS/geometry inside /app/frontend/src/components/brand/OrbitDiagram.js at ≤430px viewport width. Use this JS snippet to reproduce the failing measurement: read the getBoundingClientRect of every '.z-20' inside a [data-testid=...] figure, compare against the '.rounded-3xl' frame rect and the '.rounded-2xl' core card rect. clipped = chips whose box exits the frame; hitCore = chips whose box intersects the core card rect.
rca of the issue: OrbitDiagram uses fixed percentage-based node positions (RING={x:36,y:40}) but a fixed-pixel core card (max-w-[9.5rem]=152px) and fixed-pixel chip labels. At desktop widths the core card is a small fraction of the frame and everything fits, but at mobile widths (~350px frame) the core card grows to ~43% of the frame width and the ring's 36% x-radius can't clear it, so top/bottom chips land ON TOP of the core card. Similarly, horizontal chip labels ('Diagnose', 'AI readiness', 'Dependencies') at ~90px+ wide extend past the frame edge because 36% of 350px = 126px of clearance and the label centered on that node overshoots. Fix must be responsive: either shrink core card + clamp label width on <sm, or use a different layout (stacked list) on mobile.
